Utkam Swamy Goud, vs The State Of Telangana on 12 June,
2024
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice J. Sreenivas Rao
 Writ Petition No.32047 of 2015
Order:

entities.text: Utkam Swamy Goud, vs The State Of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
This writ petition is filed seeking following relief:
"...to issue an appropriate Writ, Order or direction more particularly one in the nature of Writ of Mandamus declaring the action on part of the respondent No.4 in interfering with the petitioner rights over the land in an extent of Ac.3.30 guntas in Sy.No.264/2 of Tadpakala Village fields, Morthad Mandal, Nizamabad District,
stating that the same is required for public purpose without following due process of law as arbitrary, illegal, contrary to the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation And Transparency In Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 and well settled legal principles apart from being violative of the fundamental and Constitutional rights guaranteed to the petitioner under Articles 14, 19, 21 and 300A of the Constitution of India and consequently direct the respondent No,4 not to interfere with the petitioner rights over the land in an extent of Ac.3.30 guntas in Sy.No.264/E Tadpakala Village fields, Morthad Mandal, Nizamabad District without following due process of law ..."

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation And Transparency In Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. No representation on behalf of the petitioner in the morning and afternoon sessions.

3. Heard learned Assistant Government Pleader for Revenue appearing on behalf of respondent Nos.1 to 4.
4.

The grievance of the petitioner is that he is owner and possessor of agricultural land to an extent of Acs.3.30 guntas in Survey No.264/2 of Tadpakala village fields, Morthad Mandal, Nizamabad District and the same was purchased through registered sale deed and his name was mutated in revenue records and pattadar passbook and title deed were issued.
5. While things stood thus, respondent No.4 without issuing any notice trying to dispossess the petitioner from the subject property and the action of respondent No.4 is gross violation of principles of natural justice and offend Article 300-A of Constitution of India.
6. After perusal of the records its reveals that when the matter came for consideration before this Court on 01.10.2015 learned Government Pleader for Revenue took notice for respondents and sought time for getting instructions and at his request, the matter was posted after two weeks.

sentences.text: However, respondents have not filed any counter nor placed any records before this Court.
8. Learned Assistant Government Pleader for Revenue submits that if the petitioner is in possession of the subject property respondent No.4 will follow the due procedure as contemplated under law.

9. In view of the submission made by the learned Assistant Government Pleader for Revenue,
respondent No.4 is directed not to dispossess the petitioner from the subject property without following due process of law.
10. With the above directions, the writ petition is disposed of accordingly.

As a sequel,
miscellaneous petitions, pending if any, shall stand closed.
